content: 1. Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB) diagnostic accuracy of Xpert Ultra compared to the microbiological reference standard (MRS) shows high true negative (TN) rates and low false positive (FP) rates across various studies. For example, TN rates of 960 with FP rates of 20 were observed in high-quality studies. 2. The diagnostic accuracy of Xpert Ultra for rifampicin-resistant TB (RR-TB) in adults with pulmonary TB, compared to MRS, demonstrated high TN rates (e.g., 970) and very low FP rates (e.g., 10), indicating strong specificity. 3. In children, the diagnostic accuracy of Xpert MTB/RIF for pulmonary TB, compared to MRS and composite reference standard (CRS), showed high TN rates (e.g., 970) and low FP rates (e.g., 20), with similar trends observed across different studies. 4. For rifampicin resistance in children with pulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 960 and FP rates of 20 in high-quality studies. 5. Xpert Ultra's diagnostic accuracy for pulmonary TB in children, compared to MRS and CRS, showed low TN rates (e.g., 970) and low FP rates (e.g., 20), with variability depending on study quality. 6. For extrapulmonary TB in adults, Xpert MTB/RIF showed very low diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 917 and FP rates of 58 in studies of lower quality. 7. Xpert Ultra's diagnostic accuracy for extrapulmonary TB in adults, compared to MRS and CRS, was very low, with TN rates of 975 and no FP cases reported in some studies. 8. For rifampicin resistance in adults with extrapulmonary TB, Xpert Ultra demonstrated moderate diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 968 and FP rates of 12 in high-quality studies. 9. In children with extrapulmonary TB, Xpert MTB/RIF showed low diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 929 and FP rates of 61 in studies of varying quality. 10. Repeated Xpert Ultra testing for pulmonary TB diagnosis in adults with initial trace results showed very low diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates ranging from 458 to 975 and FP rates ranging from 0 to 571, depending on study quality. 11. Using more than one Xpert MTB/RIF test versus a single test for diagnosing pulmonary TB in children showed low diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 980 and FP rates of 10 in high-quality studies. 12. Using more than one Xpert Ultra test versus a single test for diagnosing pulmonary TB in children showed low diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 970 and FP rates of 20 in high-quality studies. 13. Among adults in the general population with signs and symptoms of pulmonary TB or chest radiograph abnormalities, Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra alone showed moderate diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 970 and FP rates of 20 in high-quality studies. 14. Comparing two Xpert Ultra tests versus one for diagnosing pulmonary TB in adults showed moderate diagnostic accuracy, with TN rates of 960 and FP rates of 30 in high-quality studies. 15. Cost-effectiveness analyses of Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra for TB diagnosis revealed that Xpert MTB/RIF is likely cost-effective in high TB prevalence settings, among people living with HIV (PLHIV), and in settings with low empirical treatment rates. However, implementation conditions and settings significantly influence cost-effectiveness. 16. Feasibility and accessibility of Xpert testing depend on government commitment to infrastructure, stable power, cartridge supply, laboratory services, and sustainable funding. Challenges include prolonged turnaround times, limited access, and reliance on functional laboratory networks. 17. Clinicians generally trust Xpert results, but feasibility issues and logistical challenges sometimes deter them from ordering tests. Xpert's automation and convenience have improved laboratory workflows but may complicate treatment monitoring with microscopy. 18. Xpert testing cannot fully address gaps in general laboratory services. For example, disconnected histopathology and bacteriology services may hinder the effective use of Xpert machines in public sector facilities.
